body:
CHIEF PARTIAL RULING on bd-01M17004076N1E49RJ81YXMFT7 (the WOG fixture overrides the segmenter). I
am ruling the procedural half now and ESCALATING THE SCIENTIFIC HALF TO THE OWNER, because it is
genuinely not mine.

RULED, and I do not think this is controversial: THE MERGE DOES NOT BELONG IN A TEST HELPER.
Whatever the right unit turns out to be, a private function inside WarOfTheGhostsAlignmentSuite
silently redefining the unit of analysis is wrong, because a consumer cannot reproduce it, cannot
see it, and cannot tell that the published number answers a different question from the one the
library answers. Either:
  (a) the segmenter's output is the scientific unit, the fixture's expectations are restated in
      those terms, and the published numbers move -- recorded under ADR 0003; or
  (b) per-statement is the scientific unit, and the merge becomes a NAMED, RECEIPTED LIBRARY
      OPERATION with its rationale attached, available to every consumer.
Both are acceptable. The current third option -- it happens in a suite and nobody outside knows --
is not.

ALSO RULED: the ordering is backwards and that is the deeper problem. The expectations were
authored per statement, and then the code path was adjusted in the suite to match the
expectations. Expectations should be stated in terms the pipeline produces, or the pipeline should
produce the terms the science requires. Fitting the code to the fixture is how a demonstration
stops testing anything.

NOT RULED, AND I AM NOT GOING TO GUESS: WHICH UNIT IS SCIENTIFICALLY CORRECT. This is a question
about the Autobiographical Interview scoring literature and what a "detail" or "idea unit" IS in
that tradition -- whether it is clause-like, statement-like, or neither, and whether the answer
differs for source text versus recall. I can tell you what our code does and what our fixture does.
I cannot tell you which one corresponds to how this construct is scored in the field, and a chief
architect confidently picking one would be exactly the failure this project keeps catching:
encoding a scientifically wrong abstraction beautifully.

OWNER: this one is yours and it is a short question. When the segmenter splits "One of the men with
him got hit by an arrow and they lifted him into the boat" into TWO idea units -- predicate `get`
and predicate `lift` -- is that one detail or two, for the purpose of the measures we intend to
report? Our fixture currently says one, by merging them by hand, and our code says two. Your answer
picks (a) or (b) above and unblocks a P1.

m1: you own the estimand this feeds. If you think the question is malformed as I have posed it --
for instance if the right answer is that source and recall need DIFFERENT units and the merge is
covering for that -- say so, because that possibility did not occur to me until I wrote this
paragraph and I do not know whether it is real.

Unclaimed until the owner answers. Nobody should start (b) on the assumption it will be chosen.
